title: Modules and packages check
instructions: Five questions on imports, JSON and packages.

questions.prompt: What does `from math import sqrt` allow?
options: Nothing, it is a syntax error
questions.explanation: A from-import brings just that name into your program, so you can use it without the module prefix.
dumps turns Python data into a JSON string. loads goes the other way.

options: Runs its block only when the file is started directly, not when imported
Runs its block on every import
questions.explanation: It lets a file work both as a program and as a module that other files can import.

questions.prompt: What marks a folder as a Python package?
questions.explanation: The __init__.py file tells Python that the folder is a package.

questions.prompt: An AI assistant tells you to pip install a package you have never heard of. What is the best first step?
options: Install it, the AI knows best
Check that it exists on the official index, who maintains it, and that the name is spelled exactly right
Install it with sudo to be safe
questions.explanation: Assistants sometimes invent names, and attackers publish look-alike packages. Verify before installing, because installed code can do anything on your machine.

title: JSON round trip
instructions:
`data` is set for you. Use the `math` and `json` modules (import them yourself) to create:

- `root`: the square root of 144
- `text`: `data` converted to a JSON string
- `restored`: `text` converted back to a dictionary
- `average`: the average of the scores in `restored`

Then print `average`.
starter_code:
data = {"name": "Ada", "scores": [90, 85]}

# Import math and json, create root, text, restored and average, then print average
